body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\), derive a finite rule list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D\) and \(K\), whose premises use only the full signature \(\mathcal O\), current endpoint marks, \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\), and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\), and determine whether its saturation has the following extension property. For every compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\), whose observational component is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and whose \(k\in[K]\) components are obtained from faithful pooled selected laws on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), and every residual reported circle endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), there are \(\eta_{\mathtt{tail}},\eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) with opposite marks at \(e\), each a fully specified model generated by one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) and one jointly constructed kernel family satisfying non-target kernel stability across all regimes, while agreeing with every observed mark fixed by saturation and preserving every adjacency and every unshielded collider on each \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances. Each witness supplies \(P_{\eta_\star}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta_\star}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) for the observational component and, for each \(k\in[K]\), \(P_{\eta_\star,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), not a single-arm surrogate, as the faithful law of the preserved intervention-regime MAG. For each witness \(\eta_\star\) and each regime \(k\in[K]\), it must realize \(Z_k=T_k(\eta_\star)\cup((F_k(\eta_\star)\setminus T_k(\eta_\star))\cap A(\eta_\star))\), handling direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables separately rather than setting \(T_k(\eta_\star)=Z_k\). The proof may use \(A(\eta_\star)\) and \(L_{A(\eta_\star)}\) after a witness has been chosen, but the rule system may neither guess these latent objects nor invoke a global realizability query.
body.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step between conditional selected-set witnesses and a complete observable local calculus.
body.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and the discussion on p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness uncertain because no complete rules are known for their Lemma 6 background knowledge. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, proves arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG by constructing representative MAGs, but does not synchronize intervention regimes. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and the public abstract record at lines 5--9 verify a known-target enumeration-based completion; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level comparison is made. None of these sources supplies the unknown-selection common-exterior lift posed here.
body.consumer: A positive answer certifies every circle in Dai et al.'s A549 analysis; a negative answer gives a concrete obstruction requiring a richer equivalence-class representation.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct an explicit fixed finite observable rule list and prove that every residual circle has two common-basal whole-family extensions without guessing \(A\) or invoking global feasibility.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle is a development recipe, not a rule list. The proved closure only certifies a subset of every feasible \(A\); it gives no local criterion that chooses compatible unknown selection membership and one exterior DAG completion while preserving all regime fill edges and indicator colliders. The presolve draft explicitly identifies this coupled lift as unresolved.
obligation.attempted: Used intervention-created edges as observable selectedness seeds, proved the noncollider closure sound, and reduced fixed-\(A\) selected endpoints to signature-monotone reachability. These steps do not synchronize unknown \(A\), the exterior completion, and all regimes, and no permitted finite rule schema was found that does so.
obligation.partial_result: The proved certificate result gives \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\) for every compatible \(\eta\), so membership in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}\) is a sound observable rule premise.  Conditional on a fixed compatible \(A\), the empty selected subgraph and a simple signature-monotone path supply the two graphical endpoint specifications described in the fixed-\(A\) partial result.  These facts do not select a compatible \(A\), do not complete the exterior DAG, and do not provide a fixed local rule list whose residual circles certify that both choices extend simultaneously across every regime.
